section_1.title: Prerequisites: The Cone and the Plane
section_1.content: Briefly define a double-napped cone and a cutting plane. Establish that a conic section is the curve created where a plane intersects the cone.
section_1.example: Imagine a flashlight beam hitting a wall; the shape of the light depends on the angle of the flashlight relative to the wall.

section_2.title: Introducing Dandelin Spheres
section_2.content: Introduce the concept of 'Dandelin Spheres'—spheres placed inside the cone such that they are tangent to both the cone (along a circle) and the cutting plane (at a single point).
section_2.example: Visualize two tennis balls tucked inside a party hat, wedged perfectly so they touch the inner surface of the hat and a flat sheet of glass cutting through it.

section_3.title: The Geometry of Proof (Focus: Ellipse)
section_3.content: Explain the 'Focal Property.' The points where the spheres touch the plane are the foci. For any point P on the ellipse, the distances to the two foci are related to the distances to the contact circles, effectively proving the definition of an ellipse.
section_3.example: An ant walking along the rim of the ellipse; as it moves, the sum of its distances to the two 'contact points' remains constant, just like tying a string between two pins.

section_4.title: Expanding to Parabola and Hyperbola
section_4.content: Demonstrate how changing the angle of the cutting plane changes the number of spheres that can fit. A parabola requires one sphere tangent to the plane; a hyperbola requires spheres in both nappes.
section_4.example: A satellite dish (parabola) uses one focus to gather signals, while a stylized hourglass shape represents the two-sided nature of the hyperbola.

section_5.title: Summary and Synthesis
section_5.content: Conclude that Dandelin Spheres provide a bridge between the 3D geometry of the cone and the 2D algebraic equations of conic sections.
section_5.example: Using a 3D animation tool, rotate the cutting plane to cycle through Circle -> Ellipse -> Parabola -> Hyperbola, highlighting how the spheres 'dance' to maintain tangency.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisites: The Cone and the Plane", 
                          ["Conic sections result from plane-cone intersections.", 
                           "Imagine a flashlight creating shapes on a wall.", 
                           "The intersection angle determines the specific shape."])
        
        # Define basic 3D-like objects using 2D geometry
        cone = VGroup(
            Line(UP, DOWN),
            Line(LEFT, RIGHT).shift(UP),
            Line(LEFT, RIGHT).shift(DOWN)
        ).set_color(WHITE)
        
        plane = Polygon(
            np.array([-1, 0.5, 0]), np.array([1, 0.5, 0]),
            np.array([1.5, -0.5, 0]), np.array([-1.5, -0.5, 0]),
            color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.3
        )
        
        ellipse = Ellipse(width=0.8, height=0.4, color="#FF00FF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[0]))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(cone, 'C3', scale_factor=1.5)
        self.play(Create(cone))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[1]))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(plane, 'C3', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(FadeIn(plane))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[2]))
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(ellipse, 'C3', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Create(ellipse))

        self.wait(2)
